questions.question: May you overtake the leading car that has stopped at a zebra crossing?
options: Yes, if you cannot see anyone on the stripes
No, you must not overtake the leading vehicle
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 191 states you must never overtake the moving or stopped lead vehicle at a crossing.

questions.question: What problem happens if you enter a box junction without a clear exit?
options: You could block cross traffic when the lights change
Your tyres lose grip on the yellow paint
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 174 keeps box junctions clear so cross traffic is not trapped.

questions.question: When driving faster than 30 mph, what should you do when overtaking a cyclist?
options: Leave even more space than 1.5 metres
Pass closer so it takes less time
Sound your horn just before passing
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 163 advises giving cyclists even more room at speeds over 30 mph.

questions.question: How do you check the two-second rule while driving?
options: Count two seconds after the car ahead passes a fixed landmark
Leave two car lengths at every speed
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 126 explains counting two seconds from a fixed point the car ahead passes.

questions.question: What should you do with your indicator after completing a turn?
options: Make sure it cancels straight away
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 103 says to cancel your signal after finishing the turn so it does not mislead.

questions.question: What is the maximum speed limit for a car on a UK motorway unless signs show lower?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 124 states the motorway limit for cars is 70 mph.

questions.question: May you creep forward over the white line while red and amber are showing?
options: No, stay behind the stop line until green
questions.explain: Rule 175: crossing the white line on red and amber is still jumping the red light.

questions.question: What do double broken white lines across the end of your road mean?
options: You have priority over cross traffic
Give way to traffic on the road you are joining
Stop for five seconds even if clear
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 172 says double broken lines mean give way to traffic on the main road.

questions.question: You are turning into a side road and a pedestrian is waiting to cross it. What should you do?
options: Sound your horn to warn them
Give way and let them cross
Speed up to clear the turn
Wave them to stay on the kerb
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule H2 says you should give way to pedestrians crossing or waiting to cross a road into which or from which you are turning.

questions.question: Where should you position your car before turning left into a side road?
options: Well over to the left kerb
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 182 says to keep well to the left before turning left.

questions.question: What must you check before changing lanes?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 133 says you must check mirrors and blind spots before changing lanes.

questions.question: Which side of the road should you normally drive on in the UK?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 160 says you should keep to the left unless overtaking or turning right.

questions.question: At a UK roundabout, which traffic must you give way to?
options: Traffic approaching from your immediate right
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 says to give way to traffic approaching from your right.

questions.question: What signal should you give on approach when turning left at a roundabout?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 requires signalling left on approach when taking the first exit.

questions.question: When going straight ahead at a roundabout, when should you signal left?
options: Just after you pass the exit before the one you want
After you have left the roundabout
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 says to signal left after passing the exit before yours.

questions.question: In Great Britain, which way must you drive around a roundabout?
options: Either way if no cars are there
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 and Rule 186 require going clockwise around UK roundabouts.

questions.question: What is the painted box with a bicycle symbol ahead of cars at traffic lights?
options: An advanced stop line (ASL) box for cyclists
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 178 explains that advanced stop lines give cyclists space at the front of the queue.

questions.question: What does a steady red traffic light mean?
options: Stop behind the white stop line
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 175 says RED means stop and wait behind the stop line.

questions.question: How should you drive around a multi-lane roundabout?
options: Keep inside your marked lane until you are ready to leave
Cut straight across the painted lines
Straddle two lanes so nobody passes
Always drift to the outer edge on bends
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 instructs drivers to stay in their lane around multi-lane roundabouts.

questions.question: What must you do at an octagonal red STOP sign with a solid white line?
options: Stop completely behind the white line
Only stop if a car is coming
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 171 says you MUST stop behind the solid white line even if the road looks clear.

questions.question: If road arrows and signs show a different lane plan than normal, what should you follow?
options: Follow the road markings and approach signs
Always stay in the right lane
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 tells drivers to follow painted lane arrows and approach signs when marked.

questions.question: When driving past a school in a 30 mph street, what is the safest approach?
options: Drop your speed well below 30 mph, around 20 mph
questions.explain: Rule 208: lower speed gives you much shorter stopping distance if a child steps out.

questions.question: As you approach a green light that has been green for a long time, what should you expect?
options: It may change to amber soon, so be ready to brake
questions.explain: Rule 175: expect stale green lights to change so you can stop smoothly on amber.

questions.question: Why should you not wave a pedestrian across at a zebra crossing?
options: Another vehicle could be approaching from the other way
It is illegal to raise a hand
questions.explain: Rule 195 warns against waving pedestrians across because other drivers may not stop.

questions.question: When going straight ahead at a normal two-lane roundabout with no special arrows, which lane is usual?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 recommends the left-hand lane for straight ahead unless signs direct otherwise.

questions.question: At what times of day should you still watch for children near a school?
options: Any time, including clubs, lunchtimes, and weekends
questions.explain: Rule 208: schools and playgrounds are used outside normal bell times too.

questions.question: Before braking for an amber light, what should you check?
questions.explain: Rule 175: check your mirror to judge whether a vehicle close behind makes hard braking unsafe.

questions.question: When may you move off after stopping at a zebra crossing?
options: As soon as they reach the middle
Once they have crossed safely clear of your path
Before they step off the stripes
While they are still in front of your lane
questions.explain: Rule 195: wait until pedestrians have safely cleared the crossing before moving off.

questions.question: Why is overtaking banned inside crossing zig-zag lines?
options: The overtaken car can hide a pedestrian stepping onto the crossing
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 191 protects pedestrians whose view of approaching cars is blocked.

questions.question: When are you allowed to stop inside a yellow box junction?
options: When turning right and waiting for oncoming traffic to clear
When queuing to go straight ahead
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 174 allows stopping in the box only when turning right and blocked by oncoming cars.

questions.question: What should you do if there is not enough room to pass a cyclist with 1.5 metres to spare?
options: Wait behind the cyclist until it is safe to pass wide
Flash your headlights until they mount the pavement
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 163 says to wait behind if you cannot leave enough room to overtake safely.

questions.question: Why is a fixed two-car-length gap unsafe at 70 mph?
options: Stopping distance grows sharply at high speed
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 126 uses time rather than car lengths because stopping distance rises with speed.

questions.question: If you signal early, does that give you the right to pull out?
options: Yes, other drivers must stop for you
No, you must still wait until it is safe
Yes, if you signal for three seconds
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 103 reminds drivers that signals show intent and never give priority.

questions.question: What is the national speed limit for a car on a single-lane-each-way rural road?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 124 sets 60 mph for cars on single rural roads without lower signs.

questions.question: A driver behind beeps as soon as red and amber show. What should you do?
options: Move across on red and amber
Wait behind the line until green and check it is safe
questions.explain: Rule 175: never let another driver pressure you into crossing before green.

questions.question: Why should you check carefully for cyclists and motorcycles at a T-junction?
options: They are narrower and easier to miss against background traffic
They must always stop for cars
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 172 advises looking carefully for smaller, faster two-wheelers.

questions.question: Why should you not wave a pedestrian across when stopping at a junction?
options: Another vehicle may not see them or may overtake
questions.explain: Rule H2: wait patiently without waving so the pedestrian checks for other traffic themselves.

questions.question: What can happen if you change lanes without checking your blind spot?
options: You could hit a cyclist, rider, or car beside you
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 133 highlights that motorcycles and cars can hide in blind spots.

questions.question: Why should you not hug the centre line on a bend?
options: An oncoming vehicle could hit you
It is illegal to steer left
questions.explain: Rule 160: keeping left gives oncoming traffic room, especially where you cannot see round a bend.

questions.question: If a car on the roundabout is signalling left to take the exit before yours, what should you do?
options: Wait until you see it actually start turning off
Flash your lights to hurry it up
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 warns not to rely on another driver's signal alone before pulling out.

questions.question: On a spiral roundabout, how do the lane markings guide you?
options: They gradually lead you outward toward your exit
They mean you must stop on the island
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 advises following lane markings that guide you cleanly out to your exit.

questions.question: Can large lorries sometimes touch the edge of a painted mini-roundabout circle?
options: Yes, long vehicles may need to, but cars must drive around it clockwise
Only cars may drive over it
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 and Rule 188 note cars must pass around the circle clockwise.

questions.question: You are visiting from a right-hand-driving country. What habit must you watch at UK roundabouts?
options: Do not turn anti-clockwise onto the roundabout; keep left and go clockwise
Sound your horn at every exit
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 reminds newcomers that UK roundabouts always go clockwise.

questions.question: What should you do if a lorry beside you needs extra width to turn on a roundabout?
options: Hold back and give the lorry plenty of room instead of sitting alongside it
Pull right beside its rear wheels
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 and 221 warn that long vehicles swing wide across lanes on roundabouts.

questions.question: Are half-box junctions sometimes painted on only one side of a T-junction?
options: Yes, to keep that side clear for turning traffic
No, they are always full squares
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 174 covers full and half-box yellow markings at busy junctions.

questions.question: On a 50 mph rural road, why is 1.5 metres often not enough when passing a cyclist?
options: High speed creates strong air turbulence, so give even more room
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 163 explicitly requires even more space at speeds over 30 mph.

questions.question: Why is two seconds still too short behind a vehicle on a wet road?
options: Wet roads double stopping distance, so leave at least four seconds
Brakes lock faster in dry weather
Two seconds only applies to bikes
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 126 says to double the gap to four seconds in wet weather.

questions.question: A driver behind flashes their lights after you signal left. What does your signal give you?
options: No right of way; wait until the move is safe
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 103 states signals never give you priority over anyone else.

questions.question: If you drive down a steep hill, what must you watch to stay within the limit?
options: Your speed can creep up without pressing the accelerator
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 124 applies downhill too; use gears and brakes to stay legal.

questions.question: If a vehicle on the main road is flashing its headlights at you, what should you assume?
options: It is always safe to pull out
Wait until you are sure the way is clear and safe
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 172 means you stay responsible for pulling out only when it is genuinely safe.
